Relationship

Director Completion Gates are independently designed and implemented. They are inspired by Unlazy's concepts of recording acceptance expectations before work, evidence-backed completion checks, independent re-verification, layered integration checks, and remeasurement instead of trusting stale claims.

No upstream source code, template, hook, command syntax, or Depth Tree implementation is included in this increment. Because this is concept-only inspiration, the repository does not vendor an upstream license file. If later work copies or adapts upstream code, templates, or substantial prose, that change must retain the complete applicable MIT copyright and permission notice and receive a separate provenance and security review.

Deliberate security differences

The reviewed upstream security document says its checks execute shell commands with the launching user's ambient filesystem, environment, credentials, network, and tool access. Approval is consent, not sandboxing or semantic proof; referenced scripts are not snapshotted; coordination scopes and leases do not create OS isolation; and evidence can expose sensitive output.

Director Completion Gates therefore:

  • define no raw shell-command contract;
  • globally install no upstream package, skill, hook, or automatic update;
  • enable no Claude Stop hook;
  • bind runnable gates to a registered runner definition and structured arguments;
  • require shell=False, sanitized environments, bounded resources, exact repository/SHA checks, and output redaction in a later runner increment;
  • bind repository-owned scripts to exact Git blob SHAs;
  • separate manual and external-CI evidence from executable runners;
  • keep evidence outside canonical task and LangGraph checkpoint storage;
  • never treat gate evidence as review, merge, deployment, or external-write authority.

Update policy

The reviewed commit is the sole provenance reference for this design. Floating main, untagged version text, automatic updates, and production installation are prohibited. Any future upstream comparison must pin a new exact commit, review its license and security model again, identify copied or adapted material, and pass the normal exact-SHA independent review and security gates.

Canonical HTML · Director-Orchestrator · Documentation is not evidence of deployment or live qualification.
